FN-F666DC-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 429
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Kiel
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 05/09/2023
House Bill 429 as introduced would amend the Entertainment Industry Incentive Act of 2009 by
renaming it the Film and Music Incentive Act of 2023 and by increasing the production
expenditures rebate cap, the cap on state sales, use and lodgings tax exemptions, and the
aggregate annual cap on entertainment incentives for qualified production companies for
production expenditures from $20 million, currently, to $65 million for fiscal year 2024, $110
million for fiscal year 2025, and $150 million for each subsequent fiscal year thereafter. This
bill could reduce potential income, sales, and use tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund and
lodgings and use tax receipts to the State General Fund and/or the Alabama Tourism
Department by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of companies that meet the
expenditure requirement to qualify for the rebates and exemptions.
This bill would also: (1) provide for rebates to be available for production expenditures for
music albums of $20,000 to $200,000; and (2) reserve one-third of the annual aggregate cap for
qualified productions created at certain qualified production facilities located at a historic
location.

FN-F666DC-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 429
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Kiel
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 05/10/2023
House Bill 429 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would: (1) amend
the Entertainment Industry Incentive Act of 2009 by renaming it the Film and Music Incentive
Act of 2023; (2) require the Alabama Film Office to adopt rules prioritizing rebates for qualified
productions created at "qualified production facilities", as defined by this bill; (3) provide a floor
of $20,000 in production expenditures for music albums, in order to receive a rebate, as well as
a cap on rebated expenditures of $200,000; (4) limit the amount of rebates issued each year for
music album and music video productions to 5% of the $20 million annual total cap on rebates,
which would equal $1 million under the current cap; and (5) provide further for certain
productions to be meet the definition of "qualified production companies", which could reduce
potential income, sales, and use tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund and lodgings and use
tax receipts to the State General Fund and/or the Alabama Tourism Department by an
undetermined amount dependent on the amount of production expenditures rebated or exempted
from taxation for these productions that otherwise would not have been qualified productions
under current law.

FN-F666DC-5
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 429
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Kiel
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 05/31/2023
House Bill 429 as passed the House of Representatives would: (1) amend the Entertainment
Industry Incentive Act of 2009 by renaming it the Film and Music Incentive Act of 2023; (2)
increase the annual total cap from $20 million to $50 million; (3) provide a floor of $20,000 in
production expenditures for music albums, in order to receive a rebate, as well as a cap on
rebated expenditures of $200,000; and (4) limit the amount of rebates issued each year for music
album and music video productions to 5% of the $50 million annual total cap on rebates, which
would equal $2.5 million under the new cap, which could reduce potential income, sales, and
use tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund and lodgings and use tax receipts to the State
General Fund and/or the Alabama Tourism Department by an undetermined amount dependent
on the amount of production expenditures rebated or exempted from taxation for these
productions that otherwise would not have been qualified productions under current law.

FN-F666DC-6
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 429
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Jamie Kiel
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 05/31/2023
House Bill 429 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would: (1)
amend the Entertainment Industry Incentive Act of 2009 by renaming it the Film and Music
Incentive Act of 2023; (2) sunset the incentives on December 31, 2028; (3) provide a floor of
$20,000 in production expenditures for music albums, in order to receive a rebate, as well as a
cap on rebated expenditures of $200,000; and (4) limit the amount of rebates issued each year
for music album and music video productions to 10% of the $20 million annual total cap on
rebates, which would equal $2 million under the cap, which could reduce potential income,
sales, and use tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund and lodgings and use tax receipts to the
State General Fund and/or the Alabama Tourism Department by an undetermined amount
dependent on the amount of production expenditures rebated or exempted from taxation for
these productions that otherwise would not have been qualified productions under current law.
